top.reasoning: Gate checks in policy order. (1) Hard fails: critical_errors = 0, so critical_contradicted_max (0) is met. must_recall = 0.9545 >= must_recall_min (0.9), so no coverage hard fail. faithfulness_precision = 0.9828 >= faithfulness_precision_min (0.95), so no faithfulness hard fail. No Fail trigger fires. (2) Redundancy check: redundancy_rate = 0.0172 <= redundancy_max (0.15), so the length cost is not disqualifying and the coverage gain is allowed to stand. (3) Weighted score with config aspect_weights: 0.4*0.9828 (faithfulness_precision) = 0.39312; 0.4*0.9545 (coverage_must_recall) = 0.3818; 0.2*0.0172 (redundancy_penalty) = 0.00344; 0.39312 + 0.3818 - 0.00344 = 0.77148. (4) Borderline trigger: gates pass, but Must-have point K15 is Partial, and the coverage judge caps it at Partial solely because the update date 2025-01-05 is dropped from loglog L055-L059 even though all substantive content (weak performance, hot video calls, unreadable screen in direct/lamp light, average camera, paper/ink modes poorly implemented and not true e-ink, return, next Motorola G85 with G75 IP68 wish) is present. A Partial on a Must-have point is exactly the borderline-and-name-the-claim condition, so I set verdict Borderline and name K15. The faithfulness judge's lone Partial claim C033 (loglog 5.1.1) is Minor severity and does not itself trigger Fail, but it corroborates the need for human review. Concision is not rescuing any fail because none exists; with all gates passing it only served as the tie-breaker term, and its very low redundancy (one duplicate, C030 vs C001) left the score essentially at the coverage/faithfulness level. Trivia_rate 0.1897 is notable (11 trivia, mostly restated headers), but trivia is not a configured hard gate, so it appears only in the fix list.

top.reasoning: Gate checks per config pass_gates. Hard fail 1: critical_contradicted_max is 0 and faithfulness reports contradicted = 0 and critical_errors = 0, so no Critical error and no hard fail. Hard fail 2: must_recall_min is 0.9 and coverage reports must_recall = 1.0 (12 of 12 must-have points present, must_have_missing = 0), so this gate passes. Hard fail 3: faithfulness_precision_min is 0.95 and faithfulness_precision = 0.9818 (108 fully supported of 110 claims, 2 partially supported, 0 contradicted, 0 unverifiable), so this gate passes. Concision gate: redundancy_max is 0.15 and redundancy_rate = 0.0636, well under the cap, so length is not penalized beyond the weighted term. All three hard gates pass, so the sample is not a Fail. Weighted score: 0.4 * 0.9818 = 0.39272 for faithfulness, 0.4 * 1.0 = 0.4 for coverage, minus 0.2 * 0.0636 = 0.01272 for redundancy, giving 0.39272 + 0.4 - 0.01272 = 0.78. Applying the Borderline rule: gates are met on numbers, but two Partial claims, C005 (loglog 1.3, MITM threat model strengthened from 'not likely compromise' to 'defeat' with an added 'only') and C018 (loglog 2.8, encryption key model asserted as a flat definition instead of the author's hedged model with 'usually a pair of keys'), both concern core conceptual points that plausibly belong to the must-have set. Because a Partial claim touches must-have substance, I mark Borderline and name C005 and C018 rather than a clean Pass. On tradeoff, concision neither rescues nor undermines anything here: coverage is saturated (1.0/1.0) and redundancy is below max, so the length cost is justified purely by coverage gain. Highest-leverage fixes are the two Partial rewrites, since they are the only obstacles between this sample and an unambiguous Pass.
